title: Batch reservation shadowing and locality-aware drain policy
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally overcommit short-lived batch reservations in the presence of high churn and cross-zone routing. This causes noisy eviction storms during drain and suboptimal locality placement which increases p99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants. This PR introduces two coordinated features: 1) reservation shadowing for short-lived batch allocations so that transient reservations do not immediately claim global reservation quotas and 2) a locality-aware drain policy that prefers draining non-local slots first and emits additional telemetry for per-pool locality pressure. Approach: reservations.go adds a lightweight shadow buffer that holds ephemeral batch reservations for a configurable shadow window (default 30s). Shadow entries contribute to soft capacity checks but are eligible for immediate reclamation during tight capacity events. locality_drain.go implements a drain scorer that weights slots by locality affinity, recent KV cache hits, and tenant SLA class to prefer evicting non-local and opportunistic work. Both features are opt-in via DedicatedFleetConfig flags and have rollout feature gates. Telemetry: new metrics (dedicated.reservation.shadowed_count, dedicated.drain.locality_skew, dedicated.drain.eviction_reason) and a histogram for shadow eviction latency. Design tradeoffs: Shadowing reduces false positive quota exhaustion at the cost of slightly more complex accounting and a small window where global utilization appears lower; locality drain reduces cross-zone KV warmup but may delay full cluster defragmentation in extreme imbalance cases. Rollout plan: feature gated, default off for 2 weeks in prod; enable for experimental fleet pools with gradual ramp and live dashboards. Tests: unit tests for reservation lifecycle, integration test simulating churn-driven eviction, and an end-to-end perf benchmark showing 12% reduction in tenant p99 under synthetic churn. Backwards compatibility: no API changes; behavior is controlled by config flags. Related work: follows up on ENG-4219 and integrates with the warm-pool heuristics from ENG-4330. Notes: left a TODO to surface shadow window tuning in the Console once telemetry has 24h retention.
